decision.summary: The Federal Reserve lowered interest rates by 25 basis points to 3-1/2 percent to address weakening business investment and slowing global growth.

changes.quote: Today's action by the FOMC brings the decline in the target federal funds rate since the beginning of the year to 300 basis points.
changes.explanation: The Fed has now cut interest rates by a total of 3.00 percentage points in 2001 to support the economy.

changes.quote: Household demand has been sustained, but business profits and capital spending continue to weaken and growth abroad is slowing, weighing on the U.S. economy.
changes.explanation: While consumer spending remains steady, the Fed is concerned that falling business profits and weak investment are dragging down the economy.

tone_quotes.quote: business profits and capital spending continue to weaken and growth abroad is slowing, weighing on the U.S. economy.
the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate economic weakness in the foreseeable future.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.06% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.
Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, which was 4.87%, and a -4 bp move would lower the payment on a new $300,000 loan by about $8.05 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly, meaning roughly $15.00 a year less in interest on a $10,000 balance.
The unemployment rate was 4.6%, and employers have cut an average of -95k jobs a month over the last three months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.7% over the past year, while core PCE inflation was 2.1%.
Real GDP grew at a 2.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -5 bp on the day.

whats_next: The Committee continues to believe that risks are weighted mainly toward economic weakness in the foreseeable future. This educational forecast suggests the Fed remains prepared to lower rates further if business spending and global growth do not improve.

citations.detail: The Federal Open Market Committee at its meeting today decided to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3-1/2 percent.
